marble.name: 10 or 100 More or Less
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number up to 1000
marble.prompt: Can you quickly work out '10 more than 342' or '100 less than 875' in their head — knowing which digit changes and which stays the same?

cluster.summary: Your child is building number foundations — learning to read and write numbers up to 100, understanding number words, and beginning to see how numbers are built from tens and ones.

misconceptions: Changing the wrong digit (adding 100 but stepping the tens).
Failing at boundaries — 190 + 10 giving '1100' or '190' unchanged instead of 200.
Counting on in ones instead of jumping the place.
Assuming only one digit ever changes, so mishandling the carry when a column rolls over.
representations: Gattegno / place-value chart (change one row = change one digit)
H|T|O place-value counters (add/remove one 10 or one 100)
Base-ten flats/rods for the concrete +100 / +10 move
authoredAnswer: 556; 295; 705; 1,050 — changing only the right digit unless a boundary forces a regroup, and regrouping correctly across it.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: 100 more than 456 comes out as 466 or 1,456; 10 more changes the hundreds.
wrongAnswers.fix: Name which column '10 more' and '100 more' act on; add the matching base-ten piece and watch only that column (until it overflows).

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: The boundary cases give a malformed number or don't roll into the next place.
wrongAnswers.fix: Don't reteach the whole idea — rehearse the single roll on a number line or base-ten mat: 305, 295 (a ten borrowed from the hundred) and 695, 705 (ten ones... a ten makes the next hundred).
